en.greeting: Hi! Today you'll learn to join short sentences with and, but, or and because. Let's take it one small step at a time.

steps.title: And, but, or
steps.text: Let's start with three little words that join ideas.
steps.body: Use **and** (dan) to add an idea: I have a brother **and** a sister. Use **but** (tapi) for a different or opposite idea: The bus is slow, **but** it's cheap. Use **or** (atau) for a choice: Tea **or** coffee? Put a comma before **but** when it joins two sentences. With **and**, you don't need to say the **subject** again (the subject = who does it, here *Budi*): Budi gets up **and** has a shower. (*Has a shower* = takes a bath, not 'has' = owns.)

steps.title: Two ideas, one sentence
steps.text: Here are some real sentences. Look at the joining word in each one.

examples.en: I have a brother and a sister.
examples.id: Saya punya saudara laki-laki dan saudara perempuan.

examples.en: Budi gets up and has a shower.
examples.id: Budi bangun lalu mandi.

examples.en: The warung is small, but the food is great.
examples.id: Warungnya kecil, tapi makanannya enak sekali.

examples.en: The bus is slow, but it's cheap.
examples.id: Busnya lambat, tapi murah.

examples.en: Is Budi at home or at the office?
examples.id: Budi di rumah atau di kantor?

steps.body: Same idea → **and**. Different idea → **but**. A choice → **or**. When one thing happens after another, **and** is like 'lalu' (then): Budi gets up **and** has a shower.

steps.title: Build the sentence
steps.text: Your turn. Build a sentence with two different ideas.

question.solution: Sari has a car, but she doesn't drive it.
question.prompt: Arrange the words: Sari punya mobil, tapi dia tidak menyetirnya.
question.explanation: Having a car and not driving it are two different ideas, so use **but**, with a comma before it: **Sari has a car, but she doesn't drive it.**

steps.title: Or: choices and negatives
steps.text: Now a closer look at or. It has one very important job.

pairs.en: I don't drink tea or coffee.
pairs.id: Saya tidak minum teh ataupun kopi.

pairs.en: He doesn't have a car or a motorbike.
pairs.id: Dia tidak punya mobil ataupun motor.

steps.body: **Or** gives a choice: Do you go to work by bus **or** by motorbike? In a **negative** sentence (a 'not' sentence, with don't / doesn't), join two things with **or**: I don't drink tea **or** coffee = no tea, and no coffee either (like 'ataupun'). Don't translate 'tidak minum teh dan kopi' word by word: with **and**, it can sound like you only don't drink the two together.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Careful: is the sentence positive or negative?

question.prompt: Complete: Rina doesn't like cats ___ dogs.
question.explanation: The sentence is negative (**doesn't like**), so join the two animals with **or**: not cats, and not dogs either. `doesn't like cats and dogs` is a word-for-word translation of 'tidak suka kucing dan anjing'. **But** shows a different idea, which doesn't fit here.

steps.title: Because: giving a reason
steps.text: Now the fourth word. It answers the question Why?

pairs.en: I stay at home because I'm sick.
pairs.id: Saya di rumah karena saya sakit.

steps.body: Use **because** (karena) to give a reason. First say what happens, then **because** + the reason, in **one** sentence: I stay at home **because** I'm sick. Don't put a full stop (.) before because: `I stay at home. Because I'm sick.` is a mistake in writing. (In a chat, a short answer to Why? can start with Because ...) *I'm* = I am, *it's* = it is.

steps.title: Reasons
steps.text: Here are some reasons people give. Each one is one sentence.

examples.en: I like Bandung because the weather is cool.
examples.id: Saya suka Bandung karena udaranya sejuk.

examples.en: Sari takes a taxi because it's late.
examples.id: Sari naik taksi karena sudah malam.

examples.en: We don't go to the beach because it's very hot.
examples.id: Kami tidak pergi ke pantai karena cuacanya sangat panas.

examples.en: My father drinks a lot of water because he plays football.
examples.id: Ayah saya minum banyak air karena dia main sepak bola.

steps.title: Listen carefully
steps.text: Your friend Dimas tells you about his mornings. Press play and listen.

question.listen: I don't eat breakfast because I get up late.
options: He isn't hungry in the morning.
question.prompt: Listen to Dimas. Why doesn't he eat breakfast?
question.explanation: Dimas says he doesn't eat breakfast **because he gets up late**. The words after **because** give the reason.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: One more. Find the correct sentence.

options: Rina walks to work. Because her office is near her house.
Rina walks to work because her office is near her house.
Rina walks to work, but her office is near her house.
question.explanation: The reason (her office is near her house) joins the sentence with **because**, with no full stop before it. **But** is for a different idea, not a reason.

steps.title: Cheat sheet
steps.text: Here is everything on one page. Keep it for later.

artifact.title: Cheat sheet · And, but, or, because
artifact.intro: Four small words to join ideas and give reasons.
rows: I have a brother and a sister.
The bus is slow, but it's cheap.
I don't drink tea or coffee.
I stay at home because I'm sick.
tips: In negative sentences (don't / doesn't), use **or**: `I don't like tea or coffee` = not tea, and not coffee either. Not `I don't like tea and coffee`.
Keep **because** in the same sentence: `I stay at home because I'm sick.` No full stop before because.

examples.id: Rina bekerja di Jakarta dan tinggal di Depok.

examples.id: Kamu berangkat kerja naik bus atau motor?

steps.title: Learn more
steps.text: Want more? This video and this page explain and, but, or and because with more examples.

id.greeting: Halo! Hari ini kamu akan belajar menggabungkan kalimat pendek dengan and, but, or dan because. Kita pelajari pelan-pelan, satu langkah kecil setiap kali.

steps.title: And, but, or
steps.text: Kita mulai dengan tiga kata kecil yang menggabungkan ide.
steps.body: Pakai **and** (dan) untuk menambah ide: I have a brother **and** a sister. Pakai **but** (tapi) untuk ide yang berbeda atau berlawanan: The bus is slow, **but** it's cheap. Pakai **or** (atau) untuk pilihan: Tea **or** coffee? Taruh koma sebelum **but** kalau but menggabungkan dua kalimat. Dengan **and**, **subjek** (= siapa yang melakukan, di sini *Budi*) tidak perlu diulang: Budi gets up **and** has a shower. (*Has a shower* artinya mandi, bukan 'punya'.)

steps.title: Dua ide, satu kalimat
steps.text: Ini beberapa kalimat nyata. Perhatikan kata penghubung di setiap kalimat.

examples.en: I have a brother and a sister.
examples.id: Saya punya saudara laki-laki dan saudara perempuan.

examples.en: Budi gets up and has a shower.
examples.id: Budi bangun lalu mandi.

examples.en: The warung is small, but the food is great.
examples.id: Warungnya kecil, tapi makanannya enak sekali.

examples.en: The bus is slow, but it's cheap.
examples.id: Busnya lambat, tapi murah.

examples.en: Is Budi at home or at the office?
examples.id: Budi di rumah atau di kantor?

steps.body: Ide yang sejalan → **and**. Ide yang berbeda → **but**. Pilihan → **or**. Kalau satu kegiatan terjadi setelah yang lain, **and** bisa berarti 'lalu': Budi gets up **and** has a shower.

steps.title: Susun kalimatnya
steps.text: Giliranmu. Buat kalimat dengan dua ide yang berbeda.

question.solution: Sari has a car, but she doesn't drive it.
question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Sari punya mobil, tapi dia tidak menyetirnya.
question.explanation: Punya mobil tapi tidak menyetirnya adalah dua ide yang berbeda, jadi pakai **but**, dengan koma sebelumnya: **Sari has a car, but she doesn't drive it.**

steps.title: Or: pilihan dan kalimat negatif
steps.text: Sekarang kita lihat or lebih dekat. Ada satu tugasnya yang sangat penting.

pairs.en: I don't drink tea or coffee.
pairs.id: Saya tidak minum teh ataupun kopi.

pairs.en: He doesn't have a car or a motorbike.
pairs.id: Dia tidak punya mobil ataupun motor.

steps.body: **Or** memberi pilihan: Do you go to work by bus **or** by motorbike? Di kalimat **negatif** (kalimat 'tidak', dengan don't / doesn't), dua hal digabung dengan **or**: I don't drink tea **or** coffee = tidak minum teh, dan tidak minum kopi juga (seperti 'ataupun'). Jangan terjemahkan 'tidak minum teh dan kopi' kata per kata: kalau pakai **and**, kalimatnya bisa terdengar seperti kamu cuma tidak minum keduanya sekaligus.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Hati-hati: kalimatnya positif atau negatif?

question.prompt: Lengkapi: Rina doesn't like cats ___ dogs.
question.explanation: Kalimatnya negatif (**doesn't like**), jadi gabungkan dua hewan itu dengan **or**: tidak suka kucing, dan tidak suka anjing juga. `doesn't like cats and dogs` adalah terjemahan kata per kata dari 'tidak suka kucing dan anjing'. **But** menunjukkan ide yang berbeda, jadi tidak cocok di sini.

steps.title: Because: memberi alasan
steps.text: Sekarang kata keempat. Kata ini menjawab pertanyaan Why?

pairs.en: I stay at home because I'm sick.
pairs.id: Saya di rumah karena saya sakit.

steps.body: Pakai **because** (karena) untuk memberi alasan. Pertama sebutkan apa yang terjadi, lalu **because** + alasannya, dalam **satu** kalimat: I stay at home **because** I'm sick. Jangan taruh titik (.) sebelum because: `I stay at home. Because I'm sick.` salah dalam tulisan. (Dalam obrolan, jawaban singkat untuk Why? boleh dimulai dengan Because ...) *I'm* = I am, *it's* = it is.

steps.title: Alasan
steps.text: Ini beberapa alasan yang biasa orang berikan. Masing-masing satu kalimat.

examples.en: I like Bandung because the weather is cool.
examples.id: Saya suka Bandung karena udaranya sejuk.

examples.en: Sari takes a taxi because it's late.
examples.id: Sari naik taksi karena sudah malam.

examples.en: We don't go to the beach because it's very hot.
examples.id: Kami tidak pergi ke pantai karena cuacanya sangat panas.

examples.en: My father drinks a lot of water because he plays football.
examples.id: Ayah saya minum banyak air karena dia main sepak bola.

steps.title: Dengarkan baik-baik
steps.text: Temanmu, Dimas, bercerita tentang paginya. Tekan play dan dengarkan.

question.listen: I don't eat breakfast because I get up late.
options: He isn't hungry in the morning.
question.prompt: Dengarkan Dimas. Kenapa dia tidak sarapan?
question.explanation: Dimas bilang dia tidak sarapan **because he gets up late** (karena dia bangun kesiangan). Kata-kata setelah **because** adalah alasannya.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Satu lagi. Cari kalimat yang benar.

options: Rina walks to work. Because her office is near her house.
Rina walks to work because her office is near her house.
Rina walks to work, but her office is near her house.
question.explanation: Alasannya (kantornya dekat rumah) digabung ke kalimat dengan **because**, tanpa titik sebelumnya. **But** untuk ide yang berbeda, bukan alasan.

steps.title: Ringkasan
steps.text: Ini semuanya dalam satu halaman. Simpan untuk nanti.

artifact.title: Ringkasan · And, but, or, because
artifact.intro: Empat kata kecil untuk menggabungkan ide dan memberi alasan.
rows: I have a brother and a sister.
The bus is slow, but it's cheap.
I don't drink tea or coffee.
I stay at home because I'm sick.
tips: Dalam kalimat negatif (don't / doesn't), pakai **or**: `I don't like tea or coffee` = tidak suka teh, dan tidak suka kopi juga. Bukan `I don't like tea and coffee`.
Satukan **because** dalam kalimat yang sama: `I stay at home because I'm sick.` Tanpa titik sebelum because.

examples.id: Kamu berangkat kerja naik bus atau motor?

steps.text: Mau lebih banyak? Video dan halaman ini menjelaskan and, but, or dan because dengan lebih banyak contoh.
